questions.question: NSK's policy on bribery is?
questions.explanation: NSK forbids bribery in any form; gifts and hospitality follow strict written rules.

questions.question: A supplier offers you a costly gift. Do?
questions.explanation: Expensive gifts can bias decisions; decline politely and inform compliance.

questions.question: The whistleblower hotline is for?
questions.explanation: The hotline lets employees report wrongdoing confidentially, without fear of retaliation.

questions.question: Example of a conflict of interest?
questions.explanation: Placing orders with a relative's firm can bias decisions; it must be disclosed.

questions.question: Retaliating against someone who reports is?
questions.explanation: Companies must protect people who raise concerns in good faith.

questions.question: Discussing prices with competitors risks?
questions.explanation: Price-fixing talks breach competition law and can bring very large fines.

questions.question: India's competition regulator is?
questions.explanation: The Competition Commission of India enforces the Competition Act 2002 against cartels.

questions.question: India's main anti-bribery law?
questions.explanation: The Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 (amended 2018) also punishes bribe-givers.

questions.question: Insider trading means trading on?
questions.explanation: Trading shares using unpublished price-sensitive information is illegal.

questions.question: India's main company law is?
questions.explanation: The Companies Act 2013 governs incorporation, boards, accounts and governance.

questions.question: Minimum board meetings per year?
questions.explanation: Section 173 requires at least four board meetings a year with gaps under 120 days.

questions.question: Max gap between two board meetings?
questions.explanation: There must not be more than 120 days between two consecutive board meetings.

questions.question: Minimum directors in a private company?
questions.explanation: A private company needs at least two directors; a public company needs three.

questions.question: AGM must be held within how long of FY end?
questions.explanation: An AGM must be held within six months of the financial year end.

questions.question: A director's ID number is called?
questions.explanation: Every director must hold a Director Identification Number issued by MCA.

questions.question: Annual return e-form filed with MCA?
questions.explanation: Companies file their annual return in form MGT-7 (MGT-7A for small companies).

questions.question: Financial statements e-form with ROC?
questions.explanation: AOC-4 is used to file audited financial statements with the Registrar of Companies.

questions.question: Who maintains board minutes and registers?
questions.explanation: The CS maintains statutory registers, minutes and filings for compliance.

questions.question: Board minutes must be finalised within?
questions.explanation: Secretarial Standard SS-1 requires minutes to be signed within 30 days of the meeting.

questions.question: CSR spend for eligible companies?
questions.explanation: Eligible companies spend 2% of average net profit of the last three years on CSR.

questions.question: CSR applies if net profit reaches?
questions.explanation: CSR applies at net worth ₹500 Cr+, turnover ₹1,000 Cr+, or net profit ₹5 Cr+.

questions.question: The statutory auditor is appointed by?
questions.explanation: Shareholders appoint the statutory auditor at the AGM, typically for five years.

questions.question: Quorum for a board meeting is?
questions.explanation: Quorum is one-third of total directors or two, whichever is higher.

questions.question: The POSH Act deals with?
questions.explanation: The POSH Act 2013 prevents and redresses sexual harassment of women at work.

questions.question: POSH complaints are heard by the?
questions.explanation: Every employer with 10+ employees must form an Internal Committee under POSH.

questions.question: POSH Internal Committee is headed by a?
questions.explanation: The Presiding Officer must be a woman employed at a senior level.

questions.question: How many Labour Codes replaced old laws?
questions.explanation: Four Labour Codes consolidating 29 older labour laws took effect on 21 November 2025.

questions.question: India's Labour Codes took effect on?
questions.explanation: The four Labour Codes were brought into force from 21 November 2025.

questions.question: Labour Codes: normal daily work limit?
questions.explanation: The Codes set a normal limit of 8 hours a day and 48 hours a week.

questions.question: Overtime under the Labour Codes is paid at?
questions.explanation: Overtime is paid at twice the ordinary wage rate.

questions.question: Maximum paid maternity leave?
questions.explanation: Eligible women employees get up to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave.

questions.question: Permanent staff earn gratuity after?
questions.explanation: Permanent employees qualify for gratuity after five years of continuous service.

questions.question: Fixed-term staff earn gratuity after?
questions.explanation: Under the Code on Social Security, fixed-term employees qualify after one year.

questions.question: Under the Codes, wages must be at least?
questions.explanation: Excluded allowances above 50% of total pay are added back into 'wages'.

questions.question: An NDA protects what?
questions.explanation: A Non-Disclosure Agreement legally binds parties to keep shared information secret.

questions.question: Indian Contract Act dates from?
questions.explanation: The Indian Contract Act 1872 governs agreements and contracts in India.

questions.question: Out-of-court dispute settlement is?
questions.explanation: Arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996 settles disputes privately.

questions.question: A force majeure clause covers?
questions.explanation: Force majeure excuses performance during events like floods, war or pandemics.

questions.question: A liability cap clause limits what?
questions.explanation: A limitation of liability clause caps how much a party pays if things go wrong.

questions.question: The NSK logo is protected as a?
questions.explanation: A trademark protects brand names and logos from misuse and counterfeiting.

questions.question: A new bearing invention is protected by?
questions.explanation: A patent gives exclusive rights to an invention for a limited term.

questions.question: Patent term in India?
questions.explanation: Indian patents last 20 years from filing, subject to renewal fees.

questions.question: Selling fake NSK bearings breaks?
questions.explanation: Counterfeits infringe NSK's registered trademarks and can be seized.

questions.question: Pollution consent in Tamil Nadu comes from?
questions.explanation: The Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board issues consent to establish and operate.

questions.question: Before building a new line, a plant needs?
questions.explanation: CTE is needed before construction; CTO before starting operations.

questions.question: A fire NOC is issued by the?
questions.explanation: The fire service checks fire safety systems before issuing a No Objection Certificate.

questions.question: GST return for outward supplies?
questions.explanation: GSTR-1 reports outward supplies; GSTR-3B is the summary return with tax payment.

questions.question: Related-party deals need approval of?
questions.explanation: Under Section 188, related-party deals outside ordinary course need board approval.

questions.question: The DPDP Act 2023 protects what?
questions.explanation: The DPDP Act governs how organisations collect and use individuals' personal data.

questions.question: Core basis for using personal data?
questions.explanation: Personal data must be used for a lawful purpose, usually with the person's consent.
